prompt: Build a blog for Aster & Oak, a Bristol roastery: posts, tag pages and an RSS feed.

steps.title: Set it up
steps.text: One command installs kiss-ssg, adds a starter site, and points your agent at the API contract. Then add the two Claude Code plugins it prints.

steps.title: Describe the site
steps.text: Open Claude Code and say what the site is for, who it's for, where it will be hosted and its address. The skills do the rest.

steps.title: Check the build
steps.text: A dry run that reports every page, broken link and missing launch detail as data, and publishes nothing. Exit 0 means it's right.

reasons.title: Conventions, not questions
reasons.text: Folders, routes, helpers and asset names all have defaults, so an agent has fewer choices to get wrong, and every default can be overridden.

reasons.title: A verdict, not a log
reasons.text: A failed page or a link to a page that doesn't exist fails the build. Mistakes can't ship quietly.

reasons.title: Readable by the next person
reasons.text: Handlebars views, JSON models and small controllers. Whoever opens the site in two years can follow what the agent wrote.

reasons.title: A memory of the site
reasons.text: npx kiss-ssg aikb records what the site is, so the next session starts from facts rather than guesses.
